TreeHouse Foods was a direct public private-label food manufacturing comparable but appears to have been acquired and delisted in February 2026, reducing the investable public universe for pure private-label manufacturing exposure.

For this node, the investable chokepoint may be split across manufacturing capacity, packaging converters, food-safety consumables/testing, and retailer-supplier compliance software rather than concentrated in consumer brands.

node: Private-label manufacturing, specialty packaging, labeling, food safety, and retail compliance suppliers
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the private-label / packaging / compliance node found a small set of US-listed assets that sit one or two steps away from visible consumer brands: a retail trading-partner compliance network, a food-safety testing supplier, a private-label/contract packaged-food processor, and a fiber-based consumer packaging converter. The purest former public private-label food manufacturer, TreeHouse Foods, appears to have been taken private and delisted in February 2026, which increases the scarcity value of remaining public proxies but also weakens the breadth of the listed universe. This is a research universe only, not a recommendation.
